title: Tenant-scoped search query service with a DI container
name: Search query service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how the services are registered and wired together for tenant-scoped requests? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Both MetricsToken and SearchBackendToken are singletons whose factories ignore the container. Resolving them from a request scope returns what?
choices: A new instance per scope, because scopes copy the registry
The same instance every time, because singletons are cached on the root container regardless of which scope resolves them
An error, because singletons may only be resolved from the root
The same instance per scope, because scope caches are consulted first

questions.prompt: A developer calls root.resolve(IndexResolverToken) directly, outside any request scope. What happens?
choices: It returns an IndexResolver built with an undefined RequestContext
It succeeds and caches the resolver on the root for later requests
It throws because RequestContextToken is not registered on the root, but only after constructing IndexResolver
It throws because scoped services cannot be resolved from the root container

questions.prompt: Within one request, QueryService is resolved by the handler and, separately, some other code asks the same scope for IndexResolverToken twice. What do the two IndexResolver lookups return?
choices: The same instance, cached in that scope's own cache, and a different instance in a different scope
Two different instances, because every resolve calls the factory
The same instance across all scopes, because the root cache is shared
The first returns an instance and the second throws because the token is already cached
